why: The one-byte CSI, U+009B, opens a control sequence exactly like ESC plus a bracket, and VTE-based terminals, Kitty and WezTerm accept C1 controls inside UTF-8. A rule looking only at C0 misses it. The fail side is docs/a.md with U+009B encoded as UTF-8 before a colour code. The pass side is the character a cp1252 reader would have meant by that byte, the single right-pointing angle quotation mark, encoded properly: the check is on decoded code points, so the visible character passes and only the control fails.
